title: Real-Time Streaming & Vector Search Stores
description: Master Apache Kafka event logs, Apache Flink stateful stream processing, and high-dimensional vector retrieval.

questions.question: Which open-source distributed event store is widely used for high-throughput, real-time data streaming?
options: Apache Kafka
SQLite
Microsoft Access
Memcached

questions.question: Why are Vector Databases (like Pinecone, Milvus, or Qdrant) critical for AI applications?
options: They perform fast approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over high-dimensional embeddings
They replace relational databases for standard accounting ledgers
They allow streaming MPEG-4 video directly from RAM
They convert SQL queries into machine assembly code

questions.question: In Apache Kafka, what provides total ordering of message events?
options: Within an individual partition of a topic
Globally across all topics in the entire cluster
Across consumer group offsets simultaneously
Through ZooKeeper/KRaft metadata broadcast only

questions.question: What is 'Event Time' processing in stream engines like Apache Flink?
options: Processing data based on the timestamp when the event actually occurred at the source
Processing data based on the wall-clock time of the worker node executing the task
Scheduling queries to execute only once every 24 hours at midnight
Throttling event throughput to match database write limits

questions.question: What is a 'Data Contract' in modern data mesh architectures?
options: An agreement between data producers and consumers defining schema, SLA, semantics, and quality expectations
A legal licensing agreement between cloud storage vendors
A blockchain smart contract paying data engineers per query
A hardware warranty covering flash drive longevity
